prompt: Which expression is the derivative of $f(x) = x^2 e^x$?
hint: This is a PRODUCT of two functions, so you cannot just multiply the two derivatives. Use the product rule: first times derivative of second, plus second times derivative of first.

hints.text: This is a PRODUCT of two functions, so you cannot just multiply the two derivatives. Use the product rule: first times derivative of second, plus second times derivative of first.
First $= x^2$ (derivative $2x$). Second $= e^x$ (derivative $e^x$). So $f'(x) = x^2 \cdot e^x + e^x \cdot 2x$.

explanation: Product rule: $(uv)' = u'v + uv'$ with $u = x^2$ and $v = e^x$.
$u' = 2x$ and $v' = e^x$, so $f'(x) = 2x e^x + x^2 e^x$.
Factor: $(x^2 + 2x) e^x$. Choice B is the trap of multiplying the derivatives; C forgot to differentiate at all.

alternativeExplanations.title: A quick numerical check at $x = 1$
steps: Choice A at $x = 1$ gives $3e \approx 8.15$. Choice B gives $2e \approx 5.44$.
Only A matches — the product rule, not the product of derivatives.
